recommendation: Resolve all five confirmed findings and re-review exact revised bytes before any WBS build.

findings.claim: Section 5.1 closes the set of pre-charge writes to two evidence effects, but P6 makes a fresh ASC produced by a declared run_aip transition a mandatory pre-charge predicate and Section 10 assigns that AIP-pointer/ASC write to run_aip.py, so the mandatory P6 transition has no admitted pre-charge owner, state or allowed effect.
findings.disposition_reason: Confirmed missing pre-charge ownership/effect for required AIP pointer and ASC transition.

findings.claim: The Section 5.2 commit procedure re-observes only live P7-P11 predicates and re-hashes bundle inputs, while P14 additionally requires live re-verification of P13/P15/P16 non-revocation and scope and of the migration-authority receipt, so the documented charge gate never names re-checking revocation.
findings.disposition_reason: Confirmed missing explicit full P14 live authority/revocation revalidation in commit steps.

findings.claim: The post-charge invalid-ledger branch names a HUMAN-authorized repair but defines no repair state, source backup, durable candidate/receipt, allowed-effect operation, validator, or lineage rule that can admit the repaired bytes under P3.
findings.disposition_reason: Confirmed undefined post-charge invalid-ledger repair state and lineage contract.

findings.claim: The AdministrativeResourceLedger does not define how its own guarded append invocation is accounted without creating another append invocation that must itself be accounted.

A migrated base produced through MIGRATION_RECOVERY is not required to carry the fresh recovery authorization into migration_authority; first-charge admission re-hashes only the original migration decision.
findings.disposition_reason: Confirmed missing ordered recovery-authority lineage in first-charge revalidation.

residual_risks: The accepted control-write, revocation, post-charge repair, metering and recovery-lineage gaps remain until revision.
